title: private: add rollback annotations + preStop hooks for control-plane + gateway to reduce split-brain on downgrade
author: Ines Carvalho
body:
Title: private: add rollback annotations + preStop hooks for control-plane + gateway to reduce split-brain on downgrade

Context / Why
We saw a class of downgrade/rollback failures in Private rehearsals where we briefly ran two "active" instances across versions (old pods coming up while new pods still had active leases / open connections). In practice this shows up as split-brain symptoms: duplicate schedulers, competing leaders, and intermittent 5xx during the window where the rollback is applying chart revisions.

The installer rollback flow (ENG-2318) is getting stronger guardrails, but we still need chart-level behavior to ensure that when a rollback is initiated, the currently-running pods drain and exit deterministically before the older revision comes up.

This PR introduces:
- Explicit annotations on critical workloads to mark rollback ordering constraints for the installer (and for humans during debugging)
- preStop hooks + terminationGracePeriodSeconds tuning for critical components so Kubernetes terminates old pods cleanly and we reduce the chance of two active leaders

What changed
1) Rollback annotations (opt-in, chart-level)
- Add annotations to the following Deployments/StatefulSets:
  - control-plane
  - gateway
  - scheduler (if enabled)
- These are simple Kubernetes metadata annotations, not Helm hooks:
  - redwood.ai/rollback-priority: "10" (lower number = terminate earlier)
  - redwood.ai/rollback-blocks: "gateway" (component names that should not start until this is drained)
  - redwood.ai/rollback-critical: "true"

The immediate consumer is the redwood-private-installer rollback logic which reads these annotations when building a rollback plan and when deciding which pods to wait on before moving to the next component. This keeps the chart as the source of truth for component criticality.

2) preStop hooks + graceful termination
- control-plane:
  - Add lifecycle.preStop that attempts to put the instance into "draining" mode before SIGTERM completes.
  - Increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds from 30s to 90s (configurable) to allow:
    - readiness to flip
    - in-flight requests to finish
    - leader leases to expire cleanly
- gateway:
  - Add lifecycle.preStop to stop accepting new connections and wait briefly before shutdown.
  - Align terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 60s (configurable).

Both hooks are feature-flagged via values.yaml so we can enable by default for new Private installs first, then roll out to existing environments after validation.

3) Values + docs notes
- Add values under .privateUpgrade.rollbackSafety.*
  - enabled
  - controlPlaneDrainEndpoint
  - gatewayDrainEndpoint
  - terminationGracePeriodSeconds overrides
- README notes in the chart for why/when to enable.

Illustrative snippets
- control-plane deployment template:
  lifecycle:
    preStop:
      exec:
        command:
          - /bin/sh
          - -c
          - "set -e; if [ \"${REDWOOD_DRAIN_ENDPOINT:-}\" != \"\" ]; then curl -fsS --max-time 5 \"${REDWOOD_DRAIN_ENDPOINT}\" || true; fi; sleep 10"
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: {{ .Values.privateUpgrade.rollbackSafety.controlPlaneTerminationGracePeriodSeconds | default 90 }}

- annotations:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      redwood.ai/rollback-critical: "true"
      redwood.ai/rollback-priority: "10"
      redwood.ai/rollback-blocks: "gateway"

Files / areas touched
- charts/redwood-control-plane/templates/deployment.yaml
- charts/redwood-control-plane/values.yaml
- charts/redwood-gateway/templates/deployment.yaml
- charts/redwood-gateway/values.yaml
- charts/redwood-scheduler/templates/deployment.yaml
- charts/redwood-private/values.yaml (wiring defaults for private bundles)
- charts/redwood-private/README.md

Testing
- Render tests: helm template for private profile with rollbackSafety enabled/disabled
- Manual: verified that on kubectl rollout restart, readiness flips before pod termination completes
- Smoke: rollback rehearsal on staging private cluster (chart-only) shows no overlapping leaders during downgrade window (observed via leader election logs)

Rollout plan
- Keep rollbackSafety.enabled default false at chart-level for now
- Enable by default in the installer for beta customers (installer will set values for Private profiles)
- After 1-2 successful rehearsals, we can flip the chart default in a follow-up PR

CI
- chart-lint: pass
- unit (helm render): pass
- integration (kind smoke): pass

Review conversation

Connor O'Brien (Release Eng) — 2025-01-21
"Love the direction. Two nits: (1) make sure the annotation names are stable and documented (installer will depend on them), (2) can we avoid a hard failure in preStop if curl isn't present in the image?"

Ines Carvalho (author) — 2025-01-21
"Good call. Updated to treat drain call as best-effort and wrapped in '|| true'. Also added a note in chart README + kept annotation keys under redwood.ai/* namespace and added a short comment block in templates." 

Sean Gallagher (SRE) — 2025-01-22
"We should be careful about terminationGracePeriodSeconds defaults for existing installs; raising it can extend maintenance windows if something wedges. Can we gate with a values flag and keep current behavior unless enabled?"

Ines Carvalho — 2025-01-22
"Yep. Added privateUpgrade.rollbackSafety.enabled (default false). When disabled, templates render exactly as before (no lifecycle/preStop and original grace periods)."

Ethan Park — 2025-01-22
"For control-plane drain endpoint: can we define a sane default path but allow override? Also, can we sleep a bit after readiness flips to let load balancers drain?"

Ines Carvalho — 2025-01-23
"Added defaults:
- controlPlaneDrainEndpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin/drain
- gatewayDrainEndpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8081/admin/drain
and made the preStop sequence: call drain (best-effort) + sleep 10. Open to tweaking sleep values later; made it configurable via privateUpgrade.rollbackSafety.drainSleepSeconds (default 10)."

Kenji Nakamura — 2025-01-23
"Operator UX note: please ensure the values names read like 'safety', not 'experimental'. 'rollbackSafety' is fine. Also add a short comment in values.yaml describing the tradeoff (slower termination vs fewer split-brain events)."

Ines Carvalho — 2025-01-23
"Done. Added comments + linked to ENG-2318 for context." 

Approvals
- Connor O'Brien: Approved (2025-01-24)
- Sean Gallagher: Approved (2025-01-24)
- Ethan Park: Approved (2025-01-24)

Notes / follow-ups
- Follow-up PR to enable rollbackSafety by default for private profile once beta rehearsal completes successfully.
- Installer will consume the rollback annotations (redwood.ai/rollback-*) in its step graph; chart README includes a brief contract description.

Changelog
- No customer-visible change unless privateUpgrade.rollbackSafety.enabled=true (default false).
